claim: APECED/APS1 patients are deficient in AIRE, a major regulator of central T cell tolerance.
source: In 2016, in a paper published in Cell, we made at least four substantial observations concerning APECED/APS1 syndrome patients who are defined by deficiency in the AIRE gene, a major regulator of central T cell tolerance
evidence: This is stated as an established definition of APECED/APS1 patients and represents established scientific knowledge about the disease.

claim: APECED/APS1 patients share autoantibodies to a small subset of proteins, including Type I IFNs, Interleukin-(IL)-17, and IL-22.
source: i) that such patients share autoantibodies to a small subset of proteins, including Type I IFNs, Interleukin-(IL)−17, and IL-22, that was previously reported (Kisand et al., 2010; Meager et al., 2006)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous publications (Kisand et al., 2010; Meager et al., 2006) that reported these findings.

claim: Many naturally-arising autoantibodies in APECED/APS1 patients are conformation-specific and of extremely high affinity.
source: ii) that, quite surprisingly, many such naturally-arising antibodies are conformation-specific and of extremely high affinity, potentially explaining their powerful neutralizing capacity
evidence: This is presented as a finding from the authors' 2016 study, with inference about the relationship to neutralizing capacity.

claim: The high affinity of naturally-arising autoantibodies potentially explains their powerful neutralizing capacity.
source: ii) that, quite surprisingly, many such naturally-arising antibodies are conformation-specific and of extremely high affinity, potentially explaining their powerful neutralizing capacity
evidence: This is presented as a speculative explanation for the observed neutralizing capacity based on the measured high affinity.

claim: Most APECED/APS1 patients harbor 'private reactivities' collectively targeting very many autoantigens.
source: iii) that most APECED/APS1 patients additionally harbor 'private reactivates' collectively targeting very many autoantigens
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the authors' 2016 study based on their data analysis.

claim: Strong antibody-mediated neutralization of IFNα correlated significantly with an absence of Type I diabetes in APECED/APS1 patients otherwise highly disposed to it.
source: iv) that strong antibody-mediated neutralization of IFNα correlated significantly with an absence of Type I diabetes (T1D) in patients otherwise highly disposed to it (Meyer et al., 2016)
evidence: This is stated as a finding from Meyer et al. (2016) with citation to that work.

claim: The observations from Meyer et al. (2016) formed the basis for several substantial follow-up papers in peer-reviewed journals.
source: These observations formed the basis for several substantial follow-up papers in peer-reviewed journals (Rodero et al., 2017a; Frémond et al., 2017; Fishman et al., 2017)
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple follow-up publications.

claim: The 2016 paper by Meyer et al. closely aligned with contemporaneous work by Landegren and co-workers that featured a protein microarray screen of patient versus control sera.
source: Our 2016 paper discussed the close alignment of our first substantial observation with contemporaneous work by Landegren and co-workers that likewise featured a protein microarray screen of patient versus control sera (Landegren et al., 2016)
evidence: This is stated as a comparison between the two studies with citation to Landegren et al. (2016).

claim: Landegren and co-workers did not investigate the properties of the autoantibodies that were identified in their study.
source: Our second substantial observation could not be compared because Landegren and co-workers did not investigate the properties of the autoantibodies that were identified.
evidence: This is stated as a factual observation about what was not included in the Landegren study.

claim: Comparing IFN neutralization in APECED/APS1 patient cohorts defined simply as with or without diabetes did not repeat the experiment from Meyer et al. (2016).
source: In fact, the comparison that is described in the comment of IFN neutralization in two APECED/APS1 patient cohorts defined simply as with or without diabetes did not repeat our experiment.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparing the experimental design in the comment to the original Meyer et al. study.

claim: Meyer et al. (2016) compared IFNα neutralization in two patient sub-cohorts: one presenting with T1D and one not, but all of whom either harbored and/or had harbored disease-associated anti-islet antibodies.
source: Thus, we compared IFNα neutralization in two patient sub-cohorts: one presenting with T1D and one not, but all of whom either harbored and/or had harbored disease-associated, anti-islet antibodies, for example anti-GAD65, anti-GAD67, that are widely-utilized clinical indicators of T1D-risk.
evidence: This describes the specific experimental design used in the original Meyer et al. study.

claim: Anti-GAD65 and anti-GAD67 antibodies are widely-utilized clinical indicators of T1D-risk.
source: for example anti-GAD65, anti-GAD67, that are widely-utilized clinical indicators of T1D-risk
evidence: This is stated as established clinical knowledge about these antibodies.

claim: A statistically significant correlation was observed between low IFNα neutralization and T1D in APECED/APS1 patients with anti-islet antibodies.
source: Supporting our hypothesis, we observed a statistically significant correlation of low neutralization and T1D, consistent with several other experiments in which we established the capacity of APECED/APS1 autoantibodies to ameliorate immunopathology.
evidence: This is stated as a finding from the authors' data analysis.

claim: APECED/APS1 autoantibodies have the capacity to ameliorate immunopathology.
source: consistent with several other experiments in which we established the capacity of APECED/APS1 autoantibodies to ameliorate immunopathology
evidence: This is stated as a finding from multiple experiments conducted by the authors.

claim: Comparing different sera at a single high concentration (10%) is inappropriate for discriminating low versus high neutralizing activities because it will most often saturate the assay.
source: As presented to us, the comparison of different sera in the comment was made at a single [high] concentration (10%), which is inappropriate because it will most often saturate the assay, thereby failing to appropriately discriminate low versus high neutralizing activities.
evidence: This is based on established knowledge about assay design and saturation effects.

claim: At 10-fold diluted sera, no significant differences were observed between GADA-seropositive patients with or without T1D in IFNα neutralization assays.
source: This masked any significant differences between GADA-seropositive patients with or without T1D (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1A.

claim: When sera were serially diluted, the patients' broad dynamic range of IC50 values was revealed, with clear segregation of patients with and without T1D.
source: By contrast, when sera were serially diluted so as to imbue the assay with appropriate sensitivity (as described in the Meyer et al., 2016), the patients' broad dynamic range of IC50 values was revealed, with clear segregation of the patients with and without T1D (Figure 1B and C).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1B and 1C.

claim: Among 13 APECED/APS1 patients without T1D, only one patient showed low IFNα neutralization comparable to that of all patients with T1D.
source: Indeed, among 13 patients without T1D, the serum of only one ('N'; Figure 1C) showed low IFNα neutralization, comparable to that of all the patients with T1D.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: The phospho-STAT1 induction assay is an inherently less sensitive assay than the AP assay for measuring IFN neutralization.
source: The authors of the comment employed a phospho-STAT1 induction assay (Gupta et al., 2016). This is an inherently less sensitive assay
evidence: This is stated as a characteristic of the assay type, based on knowledge of assay properties.

claim: Using the phospho-STAT1 assay, at high serum concentrations, sera of APECED/APS1 patients with and without T1D showed comparable activities.
source: Namely, at high concentrations, the sera of patients with and without T1D showed comparable activities, but at lower, sub-saturation concentrations [50-fold dilutions], the cohort without T1D showed significantly greater capacity to limit IFNα activity (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: At 50-fold serum dilutions in the phospho-STAT1 assay, the cohort without T1D showed significantly greater capacity to limit IFNα activity compared to those with T1D.
source: Namely, at high concentrations, the sera of patients with and without T1D showed comparable activities, but at lower, sub-saturation concentrations [50-fold dilutions], the cohort without T1D showed significantly greater capacity to limit IFNα activity (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The experimental design employed in the comment was not appropriate to compare IFN neutralization by sera of APECED/APS1 patients with and without T1D.
source: Thus, because their measurements were insufficiently sensitive to discriminate low neutralizers from high neutralizers, we believe that the experimental design employed in the comment was not appropriate to compare IFN neutralization by the sera of patients with and without T1D
evidence: This is an inference based on the authors' experimental results showing the importance of assay sensitivity.

claim: The delayed onset and relatively rare incidence (~15%) of T1D in APECED/APS1 patients is puzzling given multiple risk factors.
source: Specifically, the delayed onset and relatively rare incidence (~15%) of T1D in APECED/APS1 patients is puzzling given that: insulin is a prototypic AIRE-regulated tissue-specific autoantigen; there is defective negative selection of β-cell antigen-specific T cells; pancreatic β-cells are notoriously vulnerable to autoimmune attack; and idiopathic T1D commonly occurs in children and adolescents (Perheentupa, 2006; Anderson et al., 2002; Wolff et al., 2014; Sabater et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies documenting these characteristics.

claim: Insulin is a prototypic AIRE-regulated tissue-specific autoantigen.
source: insulin is a prototypic AIRE-regulated tissue-specific autoantigen
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about insulin and AIRE regulation.

claim: There is defective negative selection of β-cell antigen-specific T cells in APECED/APS1 patients.
source: there is defective negative selection of β-cell antigen-specific T cells
evidence: This is stated as a known characteristic of APECED/APS1 patients.

claim: Pancreatic β-cells are notoriously vulnerable to autoimmune attack.
source: pancreatic β-cells are notoriously vulnerable to autoimmune attack
evidence: This is stated as established immunological knowledge.

claim: Idiopathic T1D commonly occurs in children and adolescents.
source: idiopathic T1D commonly occurs in children and adolescents (Perheentupa, 2006; Anderson et al., 2002; Wolff et al., 2014; Sabater et al., 2005)
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: IFN-neutralizing antibodies may delay T1D onset in APECED/APS1 patients.
source: In this context, the observations of Meyer et al. (2016) suggest that IFN-neutralizing antibodies may delay T1D onset in APECED/APS1 patients and may prevent it completely in those with very high neutralizing titres.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation of the data from Meyer et al. (2016).

claim: IFN-neutralizing antibodies may prevent T1D completely in APECED/APS1 patients with very high neutralizing titres.
source: In this context, the observations of Meyer et al. (2016) suggest that IFN-neutralizing antibodies may delay T1D onset in APECED/APS1 patients and may prevent it completely in those with very high neutralizing titres.
evidence: This is presented as a speculative interpretation of the data from Meyer et al. (2016).

claim: Longitudinal assessment reported in Supplementary Figure 7 of Meyer et al. (2016) is consistent with IFN-neutralizing antibodies delaying or preventing T1D.
source: This is consistent with longitudinal assessment, albeit limited, reported by in Supplementary Figure 7 of Meyer et al. (2016).
evidence: This is stated as supporting data from the cited figure in Meyer et al. (2016).

claim: Type I IFN is implicated as pathogenic in patients at genetic risk to develop T1D.
source: When combined with increasing numbers of studies implicating Type I IFN as pathogenic in patients at genetic risk to develop T1D (Ferreira et al., 2014; Kallionpää et al., 2014; Foulis et al., 1987)
evidence: This is supported by citations to multiple studies.

claim: Each APECED/APS1 patient is highly individual in the type and range of symptoms.
source: In fact, our observations conspicuously mirror a key clinical aspect of APECED/APS1, namely that each patient is highly individual in the type and range of symptoms; the rate and course of disease progression; and, to some extent, the time-of-onset.
evidence: This is stated as established clinical knowledge about APECED/APS1.

claim: Each APECED/APS1 patient is highly individual in the rate and course of disease progression.
source: In fact, our observations conspicuously mirror a key clinical aspect of APECED/APS1, namely that each patient is highly individual in the type and range of symptoms; the rate and course of disease progression; and, to some extent, the time-of-onset.
evidence: This is stated as established clinical knowledge about APECED/APS1.

claim: Each APECED/APS1 patient is highly individual in the time-of-onset of disease.
source: In fact, our observations conspicuously mirror a key clinical aspect of APECED/APS1, namely that each patient is highly individual in the type and range of symptoms; the rate and course of disease progression; and, to some extent, the time-of-onset.
evidence: This is stated as established clinical knowledge about APECED/APS1.

claim: Individual APECED/APS1 patients would harbor correspondingly diverse antibodies as causes and/or biomarkers of discrete clinical courses.
source: Hence, it makes biological sense that individual patients would harbor correspondingly diverse antibodies as causes and/or biomarkers of discrete clinical courses.
evidence: This is presented as a logical inference from the clinical heterogeneity of APECED/APS1.

claim: The Fisher's exact test filter would exclude 'private targets' as outliers or false positives because they are insufficiently frequent to significantly influence the distribution of reactivities across the whole group.
source: The Fisher's exact test filter would exclude 'private targets' as outliers or false positives because they are insufficiently frequent to significantly influence the distribution of reactivities across the whole group (see below).
evidence: This is based on knowledge of how the Fisher's exact test works statistically.

claim: No existing standard data-analysis method can unequivocally discriminate private specificities from false positives.
source: Anticipating this, and knowing that no existing standard data-analysis method can unequivocally discriminate private specificities from false positives
evidence: This is stated as a limitation of current analytical methods.

claim: Meyer et al. (2016) compared signals to mean and SD of controls without the additional Fisher's exact test filter.
source: we compared the signal to mean and SD of controls without the additional filter (Meyer et al., 2016)
evidence: This describes the statistical method used in the original study.

claim: Several private anti-cytokine reactivities were validated by ELISA and by LIPS.
source: First, several private anti-cytokine reactivities were validated by ELISA and by LIPS (Luciferase Immunoprecipitation – an unrelated assay platform using independent sources of target proteins displayed in native conformation), and have since been validated independently (Meyer et al., 2016; Fishman et al., 2017; Sng et al., 2019).
evidence: This is supported by data from multiple studies using different assay platforms.

claim: Anti-IL32γ autoantibodies were molecularly cloned and fully characterized.
source: Furthermore, we molecularly cloned and fully characterized such autoantibodies, for example anti-IL32γ (Meyer et al., 2016)

claim: Anti-BAFF autoantibodies were molecularly cloned and characterized.
source: anti-BAFF (unpublished data)
evidence: This is stated as unpublished experimental data.

claim: Anti-IL20 autoantibodies were detected in two APECED/APS1 patients but in none of the sampled controls.
source: and anti-IL20 (Meyer et al., 2016) detected in five, four, and two patients, respectively, but in none of the sampled controls
evidence: This is stated as data from Meyer et al. (2016).

claim: LIPS validated 24 of 31 testis- and cancer-associated antigens tested.
source: Second, LIPS likewise validated many non-cytokine targets, including but not limited to 24 of 31 testis- and cancer-associated antigens so far tested (Table 1), commonly with good correlation with the ProtoArray signal intensities (Fishman et al., 2017).
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Table 1 and cited in Fishman et al. (2017).

claim: Validated targets included twelve testis-specific and CT-antigens (PDILT, MAGE-B2, SPANXD, SPAG8, SPAG16, CT45A3, GAGE1, GAGE7B, MAGE-B1, MAGE-A3, MAGE-4 and MAGE-A10).
source: Those validated targets included twelve testis-specific and CT-antigens (PDILT, MAGE-B2, SPANXD, SPAG8, SPAG16, CT45A3, GAGE1, GAGE7B, MAGE-B1, MAGE-A3, MAGE-4 and MAGE-A10) (Fishman et al., 2017).

source: This overtly contrasts with the comment and with Landegren et al. (2016) in which the ProtoArray analysis identified reactivity to only two CT-antigens (PDILT and MAGE-B2)

claim: When the same statistical approach was applied to an independent study using ProtoArray v5.0 with 23 patients and eight different healthy controls, the overlap across the two independent studies was substantial and highly significant (p<1e-06).

(2016) but with eight different healthy controls, the overlap across the two independent studies (and platforms) was substantial and highly significant (p<1e-06), far exceeding any overlap obtained from 100,000 random permutations of patients and controls.

claim: The overlap between the two independent ProtoArray studies far exceeded any overlap obtained from 100,000 random permutations of patients and controls.
